lesson_title: Fourier Coefficients of a Rectangular Periodic Signal
lesson_core_move: Compute the complex Fourier series coefficients of a rectangular periodic signal by recognizing that only the pulse-support interval contributes to the one-period coefficient integral and evaluating the resulting exponential integral in terms of amplitude, width, period, and harmonic index.

outline_section.section_title: Reading Amplitude, Pulse Width, and Period from a Rectangular Signal
outline_section.learning_goal: Read amplitude, pulse width, and period directly from a rectangular signal plot and translate the visual data into $A$, $\tau$, and $T$.

image_policy.image_description_seed: A clean rectangular periodic signal plot with one pulse per period, clearly labeled amplitude $A$, pulse width $\tau$, period $T$, time axis, and the pulse support interval $0\le t<\tau$.
image_policy.image_generation_notes: Keep the plot uncluttered and educational: show one period clearly, mark the pulse height and horizontal width, and label the repeating period spacing. Show the pulse starting at $t=0$ so later coefficient steps can reuse the same support interval. Do not add decorative elements or unnecessary annotations.

question_policy.practice_question_model: Given a rectangular periodic signal plot, identify the amplitude $A$, pulse width $\tau$, and period $T$ from the visual data.
distractor_plan: swap the pulse width and period
use the correct width but the wrong amplitude
confuse the amplitude with the on-interval length
choose a duty-cycle value instead of the requested parameters
misread the labeled time scale or axis spacing

example_outline.worked_example_prompt: A rectangular periodic signal is shown with height $3$, pulse width $2$, and period $8$. Read off $A$, $\tau$, and $T$ from the plot.
example_outline.worked_solution_goal: Extract the three defining parameters from the signal plot without starting the Fourier coefficient computation.
example_outline.variation_from_previous: Moves from the abstract coefficient setup to a concrete visual signal with readable amplitude, width, and period.
solution_step_plan: Read the peak value of the rectangle as the amplitude $A$.
Measure the horizontal extent of one pulse as the pulse width $\tau$.
Measure the spacing between repeated pulses as the period $T$.

outline_section.handoff_notes: Use the image to make the parameter-reading task concrete, then keep both follow-up questions on the same visual-reading skill with new numbers or scales.

prompt_blocks.text: From the plot, what are $A$, $\tau$, and $T$?

answer_explanation_blocks.text: The pulse height gives $A=4$, the on-interval from $t=0$ to $t=3$ gives $\tau=3$, and the spacing to the next identical pulse gives $T=10$. So the parameter triple is $(A,\tau,T)=(4,3,10)$.
